Mete
MEET
verb
From the Old English metan (to measure, to mark out), kin to the German messen; to mete is to measure, to deal out by measure, to apportion.

Biblical Definition

To mete is to measure, to deal out by measure, to apportion with a rule. The word carries a double freight in Scripture: it names both God’s incomprehensible measuring of creation and the measure a man deals to his neighbor. Our Lord lays down the law of just recompense: “with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again” (Mat 7:2), and again, “with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given” (Mar 4:24). The rule a man uses on others God will use on him — harsh judgment earns harsh judgment, generous measure earns overflowing return. This is not mechanical fate but the moral order of a righteous God. Then the word soars: the LORD “meted out heaven with the span” (Isa 40:12), measuring the very heavens with the breadth of His hand, weighing the mountains in scales — an image to shrink every proud measurer to dust. And He who metes the heavens says, “I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth” (Psa 60:6), portioning the land to His people by sovereign right. So ‘mete’ joins two truths: the God who measures out the cosmos will not be mismeasured by man, and He holds us to the measure we deal others. Measure mercy, and mercy is meted back; measure the span of heaven, and be still before the hand that fills it.

Webster 1828 Definition

To measure; to deal or distribute by measure; to apportion.

expand to see more

METE, v.t. [Old English metan, to measure.] To measure; to ascertain quantity or extent by a rule or standard.

To deal out or distribute by measure; to apportion: as, to mete out a portion.

Used of God’s measuring of creation: to mete out heaven with the span.

Used of man’s dealing with man: the measure he metes shall be meted to him.

METE, n. A measure, bound, or limit; whence ‘metes and bounds.’

Key Scripture

Mat 7:2 — "For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again."

Mar 4:24 — "And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given."

Psa 60:6 — "God hath spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth."

Isa 40:12 — "Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?"

Modern Corruption

Not a redefined term but a lost measuring-word; ‘mete’ recovers the twofold truth — God measures all things, and metes to us the measure we deal others.

expand to see more

The word rebukes the man who metes one measure to others and demands another for himself. Our age is loud in judgment and thin in mercy, quick to mete out condemnation while pleading exception for its own. Christ closes that door: ‘with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again’ (Mat 7:2). The rule you press upon your brother is the rule God will press upon you. And behind the warning stands the greatness of the Measurer, who meted out heaven with a span (Isa 40:12) — how shall the creature who cannot measure a handful of dust set himself up to mete harsh judgment on his fellow?

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Modern usage keeps ‘mete out’ only in the phrase ‘mete out punishment,’ losing the older breadth of simple measuring. Recover the principle the word holds together: the God who metes the heavens holds us to the measure we mete to men — therefore deal mercy, that mercy be meted back.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

One old English verb of measuring, metan, still living in ‘mete out’ and in ‘metes and bounds.’

expand to see more

metan (Old English) — to measure, to mark out; kin to German messen, to measure.

mete (verb) — to measure, to deal out by measure; the KJV’s word for both divine and human measuring.

mete (noun) — a bound or limit set by measuring; surviving in ‘metes and bounds.’

The Hebrew of Isa 40:12 (takan) means to weigh or adjust by measure — the LORD gauging the heavens.

The Greek of Mat 7:2 (metreo) is the plain verb to measure, whence our ‘metre’ and ‘measure.’

Usage

"The measure you mete to others is the measure God will mete to you."

"He meted out heaven with a span — be still, and let Him measure."

"Mete mercy, and look for mercy meted back, pressed down and running over."
